items.context: When an artifact is re-committed (ON CONFLICT upsert) and the new request does NOT include a release_id (empty string), should the existing release_id be preserved or cleared? The current pattern for git_commit_hash uses `EXCLUDED.git_commit_hash` which overwrites unconditionally — so an empty re-commit clears the value. However, release_id is a cross-system correlation key that may be harder to recover if accidentally cleared.

options.label: Unconditional overwrite (match git_commit_hash pattern)
options.rationale: Consistent with every other field in the upsert. The S2D pipeline always passes all fields together, so a re-commit without release_id would be a deliberate clearing. Simpler code, no special cases.

options.label: COALESCE to preserve existing value
options.rationale: Safer against accidental clearing from non-S2D callers. Uses `COALESCE(NULLIF(EXCLUDED.release_id, ''), download_artifacts.release_id)` pattern. Adds slight complexity but protects the correlation.

items.context: The git_commit_hash addition has a dedicated test (TestDownloadHostingService_CommitArtifact_GitCommitHash, line ~530) that tests the round-trip. We need to decide how much test coverage to add for release_id specifically, since the pattern is nearly identical.

options.label: Dedicated test mirroring git_commit_hash test
options.rationale: Explicit coverage for the new field. Tests commit with release_id, upsert update, and empty-string behavior. ~30 lines of test code. Recommended because it's cheap and proves the column works end-to-end with testcontainers.

options.label: Add release_id assertions to existing commit tests
options.rationale: Less code — just add release_id to existing test fixtures and assert it comes back. Covers the field without a separate test function. Risk: if existing tests change, release_id coverage could regress silently.

items.context: There are 5 SELECT queries across download_hosting.go that return artifact columns, plus the RETURNING clause in CommitArtifact. The new release_id column needs to be added to all of them in a consistent position. The scanDest()/hydrate() helpers assume a fixed column order. Two natural positions: after git_commit_hash (grouping provenance fields together) or after release_version (grouping release-related fields).

options.label: After git_commit_hash (position 12)
options.rationale: Groups all provenance/correlation fields together: sha256, sha512, git_commit_hash, release_id. These are all fields that link the artifact to its build origin. Recommended for semantic grouping.

options.label: After release_version (position 16)
options.rationale: Groups release_id with release_version since both relate to the release concept. However, this separates it from git_commit_hash which is the other cross-system correlation key.

items.text: Codebase analysis found 5 SELECT queries from download_artifacts that need release_id added: GetArtifact (line 837), ListArtifacts (line 909), ListArtifactsForApp with is_current join (line 979), GetLatestArtifact (line 1019), plus the RETURNING clause in CommitArtifact (line 805). The COUNT(*) subquery in download_service.go:222 does NOT need changes. All scan-based queries use the shared artifactScanTargets helper, so a single change to scanDest()/hydrate() covers most of them — but the ListArtifactsForApp query (line 979) appends is_current after the standard columns, which needs careful column ordering.
